findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. 

Boxes of plastic to-go containers were observed on the floor in the backstock area where the produce department stores their containers. The PIC was shown and the situation discussed. The items were moved during the inspection to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are stored up off of the ground at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

Multiple hand sinks throughout the facility were observed with missing or cracking seals round the sinks. The individual sinks were shown to the PIC and they were instructed to repair/re-seal the sinks to the walls to maintain a smooth and easily cleanable surface at all times.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

An employee was observed to wash their hands and use their bare hands to turn off the faucet. Education was conducted and the PIC is instructed to ensure education trickles down to all employees and that they are conducting correct procedures at all times.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use.

1) In two locations the hand sinks are blocked by equipment. Locations include the produce walk in cooler and the sink at the end of the oven line. The PICs were shown and moved the blocking items to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are maintained accessible at all times to promote regulate and consistent use.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The three part sink was observed being remade during this inspection. The employee was mixing hot water with the pre-metered solution. The solution was tested and did not register on the inspector’s test strips. Education was conducted. The dispenser is designed and adjusted so that the solution coming out of the equipment is at the correct concentration and diluting it reduces its efficacy to ineffective levels. The sink was remade to correct. Ensure that education is trickled down and that all staff can use the relevant equipment correctly in the facility.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

Beef and chicken in the Asian Market are observed on the counter of the prep cooler out of temperature control. It was found that the items were removed from the cooler approximately an hour before observation. Internal temperatures were observed at 60F. Education was conducted and the items allowed to be moved back into the cooler. Ensure that foods are not left out for prolonged periods of time without temperature control.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

At several locations in this facility employee related foods and drink were observed intermixed with foods and ingredients intended for consumers. The locations were shown to the PIC and they were instructed to designate a place for employee foods to be stored so that they would not be a concern for contaminating consumer foods. The items were moved during this inspection to correct. Drinks in the facility should be in a cups that have lids and straws as well.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The sani bucket in the sushi and asian market area is observed to not register on the inspector’s test strips. The PIC was shown and replaced the buckets during the inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all sanitizers are maintained at correct concentration at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

1) The pineapple slicer in the area to the west side of the hot line is observed with dry food debris on it. When asked the nearby employee stated that they were not sure the last time that it had been used as it wasted a lot of pineapple and they have been slicing by hand for some time. This leads to the conclusion that it was not properly cleaned when it was put away and left soiled for a long period of time. 2) Multiple large buckets are used for preparing tea (per the PIC) and are stored on the shelves with remaining tea residue on them. They are also still partially wet from cleaning. The PIC had the items cleaned during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are completely cleaned prior to storage.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

The display cooler used for cake slices along the service line is observed with a holding temperature of 57F. Most items in this cooler are not TCS foods and so are not a concern. There is a box of sour cream packets in the container though that bares a label requiring refrigeration. This was discussed with the PIC and the sour cream packets discarded to correct the immediate concern. The PIC indicated that they would be putting in a work order for the cooler moving forward.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Several flies (at least 8-10) are observed by the mop sink and adjacent tanks. The PIC was shown and instructed to contact their pest control agency (EcoLab) for maintinance. They did mention that EcoLab had already been planning on starting a fly based plan in the facility. This should probably be pushed forward and implemented immediately. The normal follow-up schedule would land on a weekend and will be pushed back to the following Monday.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

Multiple rags used for wiping counters are observed stored on the counters in the facility. These items were pointed out to the PIC and discussed. They should be stored between uses in their sani buckets that are maintained at proper concentration. The rags were moved to the sani buckets to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

The hand sink in the produce walk in cooler/prep area is observed with a gap forming in the caulking sealing it to the wall. The PIC was shown and instructed to reseal prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure a that all facilities are smooth and easily cleanable where water and moisture is consistently in abundance.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

One of the doors on the employee side of the display cooler used for pasta salad has several pieces of duck tape being used as a repair medium. Duck tape is not an approved method of making repairs as it allows for mold/pathogen growth. The location was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to repair properly prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

The paper towel dispenser next to the fryers is without paper towels during this inspection. The PIC was shown and had the roll replaced during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x3) 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple utensils throughout the storage areas are observed soiled. They do not appear to have been completely cleaned prior to being placed in storage or ready for use locations. The PIC was shown each item as it was observed and the items moved back to dish for re-cleaning. This has been an ongoing observed situation for several inspections in a row and should be remedied by management. Education and oversight are HIGHLY suggested at this time. Ensure that all dishes and utensils are completely cleaned prior to storage and future use. A spot check will be  conducted moving forward to ensure that all dishes are being completely cleaned on a consistent basis moving forward.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

Multiple sani buckets in the facility are observed to either not register on the inspector’s test strips or to register low. The PIC was shown and replaced the buckets during the inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all sanitizers are maintained at correct concentration at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

The hand sink in the produce walk in cooler/prep area is observed with a gap forming in the caulking sealing it to the wall. The PIC was shown and instructed to reseal prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure a that all facilities are smooth and easily cleanable where water and moisture is consistently in abundance.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple dishes appear to have been put away with food debris or residues still present. The PIC was shown and the items moved back to dish for recleaning. This is the third inspection in a row where food contact items (dishes/utensils, ect.) appear to have this issue. A conversation with the dish washers is HIGHLY suggested. Ensure that education/training is completed and that the food contact surfaces are completely cleaned prior to storage.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Cut melons in the end cap cooler at the end of the produce section of the facility are observed with internal temperatures ranging from 48.8F-52.3F. The PIC was shown and educated on the common variability between the built in thermometers for the open sided coolers and the food temperatures in these coolers. The items were discarded during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. A similar violation was noted on the previous routine inspection. This is a repeated situation. Ensure that coolers are monitored and the TCS foods maintained cold at all times.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

1) A knife in the sushi preparation area is being stored between the prep cooler and the wall. 2) A pair of tongs are stored through the rack in the small walk in cooler next to the Asian food prep location. It is in contact with a metal section that has a white powder contaminating it. Both items were shown to the PIC and removed during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all in use utensils are stored in ways so that there is not a concern of the food contact surfaces becoming contaminated.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

From the beginning of the inspection until brought up nearly an hour into the inspection there were not any observable sani buckets available for use throughout the food prep and handling areas of the kitchen. The PIC was consulted and buckets were produced to correct. Ensure that sanitizers are ready for use at all times that foods are prepared/handled.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

A spatula in the knife rack behind the hot line is observed to still be soiled. The soiled sections are hard and appear to be remains from foods that did not get fully cleaned. Ensure that all items going through dish are completely cleaned prior to storage and use. The spatula was moved to dish to correct. A conversation with the dish washers is highly suggested.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours. 

Two knives in the produce walk in cooler are observed recently soiled and placed back in the knife rack. Also, this rack does not easily remove for cleaning and should be maintained in a clean stated. The knives were discussed with the PIC and moved to dish for cleaning.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment:
3-501.14: (A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. (B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature. (C) TCS FOOD received above 45F in compliance with LAWS shall be cooled within 4 hours. (D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less. 

Rice in the small walk in cooler is observed with an internal temperature of 84F. Rice was placed in the cooler at approximately 9 am this morning (6 hours from the time of observation). Education was conducted with the manager at this time and the rice was discarded to correct. The container was closed when observed and it was suggested to leave it cracked moving foreword to facilitate better airflow when cooling. Shallower pans and storing were also discussed.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Chicken, pizza and sandwiches in the display/open cooler to the right of the produce coolers are observed with internal temperatures between 45F-51F. Airflow and thermometers were discussed with the PIC and the TCS foods in the cooler discarded during this inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures. 

The cooler noted in line item #22 is not effectively maintaining TCS foods at safe temperatures. A follow-up is being set for 2 weeks to ensure that it is brought into compliance.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination.

Multiple moist rags used for wiping surfaces throughout the facility are observed on counters. A conversation took place with the PIC and they are aware that these should be stored between uses in the applicable buckets of sanitizer. The rags were moved during this inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur. 

A phone was observed stored in the prep cooler used for sushi prep. The PIC was consulted and the phone removed during this inspection to correct. Ensure that personal items are stored away from foods and food prep areas.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

Multiple hand sinks throughout the facility are blocked during this inspection. PIC was consulted and the items removed to correct. PIC is aware that all hand sinks should be maintained easily accessible at all times.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

The hand sink next tot he pizza preparation area is observed with significant food debris inside of it, leading to the conclusion that it was used as a dump sink. PIC was consulted and the sink cleaned. Ensure that the hand sinks are used for no other purpose other than hand washing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

Multiple buckets of sanitizer in the prep/service areas would not produce a color change on inspector test strips. Buckets were remade during this inspection to correct the violation. Buckets should be changed at a frequency so that they do not fall bellow effective levels at any time.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

1) Multiple sets of utensils (knives, tongs, spatulas and cutting boards) throughout the foods preparation/handling areas are observed stored for use, but still soiled. PIC is instructed to discuss with the dish washers and ensure that all dishes are cleaned completely prior to storage for use. The noted items were moved to dish for re-cleaning. 2) Multiple pans are observed on the hot line with residual food debris/grease from the night before. Items were discussed with the PIC and moved to dish for cleaning.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

Knives observed stored in the knife racks in the Hychi area as well as behind the market grill are soiled and the inside of the racks (food contact surface contacting) are observed soiled with food debris. The utensils as well as the racks should be maintained clean and in a state so that they remain clean and do not contaminate each other throughout storage and use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

Multiple gaps between the wells in the steam table in the market grill area are observed with accumulated food residue. PIC is instructed to clean often enough so as to prevent accumulation in these gaps.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

Multiple buckets of sanitizer in the prep/service areas would not produce a color change on inspector test strips. Buckets were remade during this inspection to correct the violation. Buckets should be changed at a frequency so that they do not fall bellow effective levels at any times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-702.11: UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning. 

The setting used a the beginning of the inspection for the dish machine only allowed for a sanitizing temperature of 144F-146F. Dishes must reach a surface temperature of 160F minimum for effective sanitization. Changing the setting from one to two brought the rinse temperature up to 168F and corrected the violation. Ensure that dishes are effectively sanitized when washed.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

The far bottom right section of the produce retail coolers (nearest to the registers) is holding cut watermelons between 46F-60F. PIC was consulted and multiple items probed. Only the bottom shelf for approximately 2-3 feet appears to be out of compliance. The TCS foods in this area were discussed during this inspection and discarded to correct the violation. Per the PIC this area normally does not hold TCS items. They are instructed to either return the area to only non-TCS items or have the cooler adjusted to maintain foods at 41F or less.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. 

A spray bottle with a dark blue solution (identified as glass cleaner) is in a bottle labeled as sanitizer. PIC was consulted and the bottle discarded during this inspection. Ensure that chemicals used in the facility bear accurate labels

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

The scoops used for scooping cooked rice are currently stored between uses in standing water. PIC is instructed to store them in one of the above ways to provide for food safety.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

The container of scoops/spatulas for the cold service area are observed with both the food contact and handles intermixed. PIC is instructed to maintain the container so that the food contact surfaces remain down in the bucket. Items were rearanged during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation. 

The sushi cooler has a drip that is currently being managed by a rag absorbing the water. Per the PIC a work order has already been submitted. This situation was noted in the general comments of the previous routine inspection. PIC is instructed to ensure that the equipment is repaired prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment: Sushi HACCP logs are not being properly maintained. Staff did not demonstrate knowledge of sushi rice preparation and pH testing procedures. Train employees and ensure logs are properly maintained. Inspector will follow up in 30 days.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11 The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (N) EMPLOYEES are properly trained in FOOD; and (P) Written procedures and plans are maintained and implemented as required. [Pf]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Employee observed to turn faucet off and dispense paper towels without the use of a barrier after washing hands. CORRECTED- Provided education and discussed with PICs.
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
No paper towels available at two handwashing sinks throughout the kitchen. CORRECTED- PIC replaced paper towels upon request. Ensure towels are always available.
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Shell eggs observed stored above produce in the ASIAN prep cooler. CORRECTED- Discussed with PICs, who provided education. Potentially contaminated foods were voluntarily discarded.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Sanitizer buckets in the SUSHI and PRODUCE areas observed with low/no measurable concentration of quat. Wall-mounted dispensers in both areas were observed without any sanitizer concentrate remaining in the bulk container. CORRECTED- Both dispensers were supplied with sanitizer. Buckets were remade for service areas.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114 (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have a concentration based on label. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment:
Sushi rice observed to be 112F probed at 11AM. Two hours later at 1PM, sushi rice was observed to be 90F. CORRECTED- Since documentation showing proper acidification, sushi rice was voluntarily discarded.
3-501.14: (A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. (B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature. (C) TCS FOOD received above 45F in compliance with LAWS shall be cooled within 4 hours. (D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Meatballs in the ITALIAN prep cooler observed dated 9/13. Use or discard foods within 7 days of preparation/opening the package. CORRECTED- Food was voluntarily discarded.
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. [P]

findings.title: Compliance with variance/specialized process/HACCP
findings.comment:

[Pf]

Mashed potatoes observed at 120F (probed). CORRECTED— Discussed with PIC. Mashed potatoes will be rapidly reheated to 165F, or must be discarded.

findings.title: Compliance with variance/specialized process/HACCP
findings.comment:
Review of sushi pH records indicate that sushi rice has had a pH of 7 for at least the last month prior to this inspection. Facility is in the process of replacing their existing pH testing supplies. Review pH testing procedures and HACCP requirements with staff. According to HACCP plan, sushi rice pH must be between 3.6 and 4.1. If pH is outside of this range, corrective actions must be taken.
8-103.12: If AUTHORITY grants VARIANCE, PERMIT HOLDER shall: (A) comply with HACCP PLAN (P) (B) Maintain and provide records. [Pf]

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.820 -Buildup was once again observed on the surfaces of the juicing machine where oranges come in contact with the equipment. The main area of concern being the front rotating parts that are under the clear removable cover. White grimy buildup was present. Parts were removed to be cleaned and sanitized during the inspection. 

Properly clean and sanitize the juicing machine between uses. Remove all detachable parts to be manually washed, rinsed, and sanitized at the 3 part sink. Make sure all stationary components are also properly cleaned and sanitized prior to placing removable parts back on the machine.
NOTE: The top of the machine with the detachable black plate was observed to be clean.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750.830g - Quat test kit could not be located in the salad bar prep area during the inspection. Staff on duty also appeared unfamiliar with the concept of sanitizer test strips. Staff on duty were educated as to the need/purpose of test strips. Manager on duty stated a new set of quat strips would be obtained for the area. Assistant Manager was advised to work with the Salad Bar Manager to provide additional education and training on proper cleaning/sanitizing and the use of test strips.

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.820 -Buildup was observed on various surfaces of the juicing machine where oranges come in contact with the equipment. Assistant Manager removed some parts for cleaning but was not certain how all of the components are typically handled for ware washing. The machine would not be used any more today and would be properly cleaned and sanitized prior to the next use, which would possibly be tomorrow morning. Assistant Manager stated he would contact the Salad Bar Manager regarding the need for proper wash/rinse/sanitize before use.

Properly clean and sanitize the juicing machine between uses. Remove all detachable parts to be manually washed, rinsed, and sanitized at the 3 part sink. Make sure all stationary components are also properly cleaned and sanitized prior to placing removable parts back on the machine.
NOTE: Spot check may be conducted at any time to check on the cleaning/sanitizing process for the juicing machine.

750.1120 - Handsink in trim room was soiled with buildup. Clean handsinks and related fixtures daily/as needed, and maintain them clean.

Handsinks and related fixtures shall be maintained clean and in good repair.
NOTE: Make sure handsinks are accessible at all times, and reiterate handwashing prior to produce prep with staff that work in the trim room.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed 3 knives, in 2 separate knife racks, being stored dirty with food debris on them. Employee admitted to having not used one of the knives today and the other 2 knives were uncertain. Ensure that, if a utensil is contaminated or soiled, it is washed, rinsed, and sanitized prior to placing it into the clean knife rack. Knives were removed for cleaning during the inspection. 
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800(e) Observed the exterior and interior of the cabinets under the prep table in the salad bar prep room to be soiled with food debris. Clean and maintain non-food contact surfaces.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1220 Observed the the floor underneath the shelving unit holding clean and sanitized equipment to be soiled with a sticky substance/food splash. Floors shall be cleaned and maintained to avoid providing food, water, and harborage for pests.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: The melon does not have correct time on the tag. The tags have a time stamp but it was not the correct time. Fresh squeezed juice is observed to be placed into the cooler to cool with no time tag. 750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F. Place time on potentially hazardous items and ensure that they are properly cooled to 41F or below.  The employee stated that at times they take melons off of the shelf, cut and place out in the cold unit for sale with no pre chill step.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: Cut melon on an end cap open top cooler at 54F. 750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above) The cut melons were discarded in the garbage. These melons were (according to the employees) cut in the trim room and cooled over night in the cooler, Cooler temperature was 34F. The melons were placed on the end cap unit at around 6am. Give attention to the type of unit used for the type of product.  Air temp on the unit is 35F according to the internal thermometer.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text: 750.140(a) Trim room does not have a thermometer. See notes in the General Comments. Provide a thermometer within this room and educate staff to monitor the temperature. Make sure they know who is to be notified should the thermometer indicate over 41F. All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided

Provide test strips for all dispensing units. Make sure staff is educated on how the strips are used.  A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.
